decisions.reason: The preceding question explicitly concerns the power connector. The signal connector and its seven-pin signal pinout remain unchanged.
Changing the physical order of pins on the matched power connectors does not alter I2C speed, pull-ups, cable length, or pull-up location.
The source decision concerns the power connector pin order and does not change the USB D+ and D- data-line requirement.
Permission to choose the power-connector pin order for layout convenience does not change any established board dimensions, orientation, mounting, placement, clearance, or spacing constraint.
The source concerns the interboard power connector, not the separate battery connector or its JST-PH pin requirements.
Flexible ordering of interboard power pins does not change the required four-layer stack.
The interboard power-connector pin order does not alter charge-status indication through the main-board SK6812 LED chain.
The source does not change battery protection thresholds, thermal sensing, or the NTC connection.
Reordering matched power-connector pins does not change generation, enable control, default state, or use of the switched 5V rail.
The source permits layout-driven pin ordering but does not select a different component or revise any sourceability policy.
The requirement for a three-board architecture remains unchanged by a pin-order adjustment to one interboard connector.
The power-connector pin-order decision does not affect ESP32 clocking, sleep policy, or wake sources.
